article_title: Does seniority always correlate with simulated intubation performance? Comparing endotracheal intubation performance across medical students, residents, and physicians using a high-fidelity simulator.
citation: Yau Sze-Yuen, Chang Yu-Che, Wu Meng-Yu, Liao Shu-Chen. (2021). Does seniority always correlate with simulated intubation performance? Comparing endotracheal intubation performance across medical students, residents, and physicians using a high-fidelity simulator. PLoS ONE. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0257969
title: Kyoto Kagaku MW11 difficult airway management simulator evaluation system
description: The MW11 DAM simulator is a high-fidelity airway training and assessment device used as the study's measurement platform. It presents four graded scenarios — normal airway, locked jaw, rigid neck and micrognathia — and records success, intubation time, peak force on incisor and tongue, and Cormack Lehane grade. The authors note it "was developed at Waseda University in 2006 to serve as an active training device and as an advanced evaluation tool for surgical instruments and medical procedures."
requirements: Learners must be familiarized with the devices before assessment; the study used a 30-minute device familiarization section.
constraints: The authors could not find English literature describing verification of the simulator's Cormack Lehane grade algorithm, and measured forces were higher than in previous studies, possibly due to the simulator's force-measurement setup.
target_learning_goals: Assessment of intubation performance across devices and scenarios
examples: Each participant performed 12 intubations (4 scenarios × 3 devices: direct laryngoscopy, Trachway, Glidescope) assessed on the MW11.
